timing_rule: Latest eligible year per source within 3 years; dated fieldwork must end before the decision, otherwise an earlier calendar year is required. Retain all eligible question variants in that year.

admissions.support_definition: General affirmative-action support; source-specific combined populations and policy areas make this contextual only.

admissions_diversity.support_definition: Race and ethnicity in selective-college admissions for diversity; contextual to the specific challenged programs.

admissions_earlier.support_definition: Separate campus-representation and admissions-criteria questions; original categories retained without a combined support score.

cases.name: Fisher v. University of Texas (2013)

components.decision: Vacated and remanded for application of proper strict scrutiny.
components.scope: The Court resolved the review standard without finally deciding whether this admissions plan was lawful.
components.locator: Kennedy majority opinion Part III and closing paragraph.
components.survey_fit: General affirmative-action preferences do not decide how a court should apply strict scrutiny.

cases.interpretation_limit: This is not a final yes/no ruling on the program. The procedural label here refers to that policy comparison, not an absence of legal substance.

cases.name: Fisher v. University of Texas (2016)

components.decision: Upheld the challenged race-conscious admissions plan under equal protection.
components.scope: Race as one factor in holistic review alongside a percentage-admission pathway; the Court upheld this particular program and record, not every racial preference.
components.survey_fit: Pew asks about increasing campus representation; Gallup asks about considering race against a merit-only alternative. Both concern higher education, but neither describes Texas’s percentage pathway, holistic review, or constitutional test. Keep the two questions separate and contextual.

observations.wording: Choosing admission based only on merit despite low minority enrollment, or considering race and ethnicity for diversity even if some minority applicants otherwise would not be admitted.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased summary. The rotated alternatives frame a trade-off between merit and racial/ethnic consideration; this is survey wording, not the app’s claim that the two are mutually exclusive. National weighted results include oversamples of Black and Hispanic adults recontacted from Gallup Daily. Fieldwork straddles Fisher I (2013), so it cannot serve as earlier opinion for that ruling.
observations.weight: Published weighted national telephone-survey topline; no recalculation.
observations.denominator: National sample of 4,373 adults; uncertainty retained in the published categories.
observations.orientation: Policy preferences under this wording, not approval of Fisher or its constitutional reasoning.

observations.wording: Whether affirmative-action programs intended to increase Black and minority representation on college campuses are good or bad.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased summary. Asked all respondents. This describes a representation goal, not explicit race-based selection criteria or the Texas program. Published percentages total 101 because of rounding; do not calculate uncertainty as the residual 7%.
observations.weight: Published weighted national telephone-survey topline; no recalculation.
observations.denominator: National sample of 3,335 adults; uncertainty retained in the published categories.
observations.orientation: Policy preferences under this wording, not approval of Fisher or its constitutional reasoning.

cases.interpretation_limit: Different wording, years and survey designs prevent interpreting the percentages as a trend or an isolated wording effect. The 2013 Gallup and 2014 Pew fieldwork preceded Fisher II; Gallup’s June–July 2016 survey straddled the decision and is not used.

cases.name: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard / UNC

components.decision: Invalidated the challenged race-conscious admissions programs.
components.scope: Limits those uses of race; does not prohibit considering an individual’s account of how race affected their life. Military academies were not decided.
components.locator: Roberts majority opinion Parts III–VI; footnote 4.
components.survey_fit: VOTER combines women and racial minorities and does not specify admissions. Its 2020 responses do not directly measure approval of the 2023 holdings.

observations.wording: Do you generally favor or oppose affirmative action programs for women and racial minorities?
observations.denominator: Positive-weight administered-wave answers, including unsure/skipped; not-asked/system missing excluded. The question combines women and racial minorities and does not isolate college admissions.

components.decision: Invalidated the challenged race-conscious admissions programs.
components.scope: Limits those uses of race; does not prohibit considering an individual’s account of how race affected their life. Military academies were not decided.
components.locator: Roberts majority opinion Parts III–VI; footnote 4.
components.survey_fit: The question isolates race and ethnicity in selective-college admissions for diversity. It does not describe Harvard’s or UNC’s particular programs, so this remains context rather than a case-approval estimate.

observations.wording: Considering race and ethnicity in selective-college admissions to increase student diversity.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased summary. Asked all Wave 125 respondents. The question describes admissions and diversity specifically, but does not describe the Harvard or UNC programs. Methodology and full topline are in the report.
observations.weight: Published weighted American Trends Panel topline; no recalculation.
observations.denominator: All 5,079 U.S. adults in the probability-based online panel survey; not sure and no answer retained.
observations.orientation: Approval of the described admissions policy, not approval of the constitutional reasoning.

cases.interpretation_limit: The two companion cases are one displayed event, not two independent survey comparisons. Broad affirmative-action opinion cannot establish exact-case agreement.

limitations: Explicit source-based legal coding is an input, not an automated legal classifier.
Contextual matches do not measure approval of the specific holding.
Mixed and unresolved components retain their labels; no scalar direction is inferred.
No pooling, confidence intervals, causal claims, or prediction.
